chunks: With this chain of transmission, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from a number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from Muḥammad ibn Ismāʿīl, who said:

I asked al-Riḍā عليه السلام about a man who has intercourse with a woman near the private part, and neither of them emits semen: when does ghusl become obligatory? He said: When the two circumcised parts meet, then ghusl has become obligatory. I said: Is the meeting of the two circumcised parts the disappearance of the glans? He said: Yes.

key_terms.الْتَقَى الْخِتَانَانِ: the meeting of the two circumcised parts, the legal threshold mentioned for ghusl
key_terms.الْغُسْلُ: ritual bath that becomes obligatory after certain acts, including qualifying sexual intercourse
key_terms.غَيْبُوبَةُ الْحَشَفَةِ: the disappearance of the glans, clarifying the meaning of the legal threshold

ai.seo_question: When does ghusl become obligatory if intercourse occurs without ejaculation?
ai.summary: This hadith states the legal criterion for the obligation of ghusl in sexual intercourse, even when ejaculation does not occur. It clarifies that ghusl becomes obligatory upon the meeting of the circumcised parts, explained here as the disappearance of the glans.
